evals.prompt: I have a GitLab merge request (iid 128) in project group/project. Write a bash snippet using glab that posts an inline review comment anchored to line 42 of src/api/users.go — a line that was ADDED in this MR — by calling the raw Discussions REST API (not the glab convenience subcommand), and make sure the comment actually attaches to the diff rather than floating on the Overview tab.
assertions: The position object sets all three of base_sha, start_sha, and head_sha (fetched from the MR diff_refs or versions endpoint)
It sets position new_line (for the added line) and both old_path and new_path, and does NOT set old_line for the added line
After the POST it verifies the created note type equals DiffNote (e.g. checks notes[0].type == "DiffNote") rather than trusting the 201 status

evals.prompt: We run a GitLab CI job that should automatically open a merge request and post review comments on it. Which token should the job use and what scope does it need? Explain what will and won't work.
assertions: States that CI_JOB_TOKEN is read-only on merge requests and cannot create MRs or post notes, so a PAT or project/group access token must be used instead
States that writing (create MR / post comment) requires the broad api scope, and that read_api is read-only / write_repository does not cover discussions

evals.prompt: Using glab, how do I publish a code review on a GitLab MR that has a summary plus two inline findings, and mark the review as requesting changes so the MR can't be merged until addressed? Give the commands.
assertions: Makes clear there is no single atomic review object / no REST REQUEST_CHANGES: the summary is a plain note, each inline finding is its own discussion, and the verdict is separate
Implements blocking by withholding approval and/or leaving threads unresolved (relying on only_allow_merge_if_all_discussions_are_resolved), not by a REQUEST_CHANGES call

evals.prompt: On GitLab, how do I programmatically resolve a specific review discussion thread on a merge request once the finding is fixed? Show the API call.
assertions: Uses a REST PUT to the discussions endpoint with resolved=true (e.g. PUT .../discussions/<discussion_id>?resolved=true) and does not require GraphQL
Identifies the thread by its discussion id rather than by line number

evals.prompt: Onboard mandatory governance checks and protected production releases across our GitLab group. We want reusable components rather than copied YAML, immutable dependencies, typed inputs and component tests, central policy injection that projects cannot omit, safe merge/name semantics, compliance scope, protected deployment approval, preview/rollback, and evidence. Explain the design and bypass tests.
assertions: Uses a full-SHA-pinned CI/CD component with typed inputs, configurable unique job names/stages, nested dependency review, and component-project tests covering missing inputs and duplicate inclusion

Uses a protected security-policy project plus pipeline execution policy for mandatory injection, documents project/project-policy/group-policy merge order and deliberate suffix on_conflict versus suffix never behavior, and tests omitted project CI plus name/variable conflicts
Uses compliance frameworks only for native classification/control/reporting and explicitly rejects treating framework assignment as certification or proof of legal compliance
Protects release/deployment targets and environments with eligible approval, least-privilege credentials, exact commit/artifact binding, and pipeline/job/artifact/deployment evidence
Uses discover, rendered preview, authorize, apply, authoritative re-read/negative-probe verify, rollback, and drift steps without requiring an agent harness or lifecycle module
